issues.description: Class GroverTwoQubitWithoutAuxiliaryQubit constructor signature differs between template and solution and conflicts with the problem statement. In the template (template_repository/ex1_grover_two_qubit_without_auxiliary_qubit.py) the constructor is declared as def __init__(self, num_qubits: int): which requires a parameter named num_qubits. In the solution (solution_repository/ex1_grover_two_qubit_without_auxiliary_qubit.py) the constructor is parameterless: def __init__(self): and sets the fixed two-qubit configuration (self.number_of_qubits_query_register = 2). The problem statement (problem_statement.md, Exercise 1) describes a fixed two-qubit exercise (searching for |11>). This mismatch can confuse students about how to instantiate the class (whether to pass an argument) and what value to provide, and it may lead to inconsistencies when following the provided solution or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent with the exercise intent. Options: (A) Change the template constructor to def __init__(self): and set self.number_of_qubits_query_register = 2 (with explanatory docstring stating the exercise uses a fixed two-qubit circuit), or (B) accept a num_qubits parameter with a sensible default def __init__(self, num_qubits: int = 2): and use that value to initialize self.number_of_qubits_query_register. Update the template docstring to state whether the class expects an explicit argument or uses the default so students are not confused.
